items.description: `iac-image` no longer rebuilds on pushes that cannot change the image: a push touching only roles, playbooks, host_vars or Terraform `.tf` leaves the build a no-op — the stage reports skipped for conditional and no `registry:5000/iac` tag is pushed.
items.rationale: Static: imageBuildRequired() (Jenkinsfile.iac-image) is a plain boolean OR of six utils.hasChanges(...) full-match regexes; read directly, and independently checked against the shared library source (vars/utils.groovy:33-41 via gitblit) confirming `it.path ==~ pattern` is Groovy full-match, so an unwatched path never trips it. Live: the commit that lands this gate necessarily touches Jenkinsfile.iac-image itself (a watched input), so pushing this slice could only ever exercise the BUILD path, not the skip path -- exactly as PA's done-record predicted. Observed: push of d1005fa triggered IaC/IaC Docker Image #122 (SUCCESS, 209s) which ran a real kaniko build (COPY support/iac-image/terraform.rc, COPY ansible/files/known_hosts.d/homelab, etc.) and pushed both tags -- the non-skip path end to end. The skip path itself (an unrelated push touching none of the six patterns) cannot be observed from inside this slice by construction; it is proven the next time an unrelated Ansible push lands, which is routine future traffic, not owed work.
evidence: https://jenkins.webathome.org/job/IaC/job/IaC%20Docker%20Image/122/ -- SUCCESS, 209s, real build+push observed for commit d1005fa

items.area: Pillar A — the input set (R1, ruling)
items.description: A push touching any real image input still rebuilds and pushes both tags exactly as before. The input set is the one the Dockerfile as it stands defines — `support/iac-image/**`, the root `pyproject.toml`/`poetry.lock`, `ansible/roles/baseline/files/homelab-root.crt`, `ansible/files/known_hosts.d/homelab` — and nothing outside it reaches the image.
items.rationale: Read support/iac-image/Dockerfile in full this pass: the only COPYs are terraform.rc (:the build's own context), homelab-root.crt, known_hosts.d/homelab, the root pyproject.toml/poetry.lock, the build-stage binary (:25) and a pinned external image (:129) -- nothing else reaches the image. Confirmed only one pyproject.toml/poetry.lock exist in the repo (root), so the unqualified patterns are unambiguous. Live: build #122's kaniko log shows exactly 'COPY support/iac-image/terraform.rc', 'COPY ansible/files/known_hosts.d/homelab', both tags (registry:5000/iac:122 and :latest) pushed at the same digest -- the same set the Dockerfile as it stands defines.
evidence: https://jenkins.webathome.org/job/IaC/job/IaC%20Docker%20Image/122/ console log lines 1567-1590 (the COPYs and both pushed tags, same sha256 digest)

items.area: Pillar A — the provider is not an input (ruling)
items.description: The provider drops off the input list: no provider artifact is baked into or copied into the image, and a provider release alone does not rebuild it.
items.rationale: support/iac-image/terraform.rc:1-9 declares only a network_mirror at tfmirror.home -- no filesystem_mirror block, so nothing bakes a provider binary into the image. Jenkinsfile.iac-image has no copyArtifacts step (full file read). Build #122's kaniko log confirms no provider-related COPY.

items.area: Pillar A — gate inside the pipeline (R2)
items.description: The gate is inside the pipeline, not in the job's trigger: the push trigger is left alone and the build is made a no-op when no image input changed, using the same `utils.hasChanges(...)` / `markStageSkippedForConditional` pattern HelmCharts already uses.
items.rationale: Diffed against /work/HelmCharts/Jenkinsfile and /work/DockerImages/Jenkinsfile directly (both checked out locally): same org.jenkinsci...Utils import, same Utils.markStageSkippedForConditional(...) call in the else branch, same utils.hasChanges(...) shape. The push trigger itself is untouched (no changes to job-level config; the gate is inside the pipeline script only). checkout scm (Jenkinsfile.iac-image:8) is intact, which the changeset read depends on.
evidence: Jenkinsfile.iac-image:5-7 (checkout scm, which the changeset read depends on)

items.area: Pillar A — the gate's patterns full-match (ruling)
items.description: Every path the gate watches is written so it full-matches: each pattern matches the whole repo-relative path of the input it names — a directory prefix carries an explicit trailing `/.*` — so no image input is silently unwatched and the gate does not skip every build.
items.rationale: Read JenkinsPipelineUtils vars/utils.groovy:33-41 directly via the gitblit mirror this pass (not taken on the plan's citation alone): `it.path ==~ pattern` is Groovy's full-match operator. All six of Jenkinsfile.iac-image's patterns are either a bare literal file path (Jenkinsfile\.iac-image, pyproject\.toml, poetry\.lock, the two ansible/... file paths -- each with escaped literal dots) or a directory prefix with an explicit trailing /.* (support/iac-image/.*), matching the sibling repos' shape exactly. Confirmed the repo holds exactly one pyproject.toml/poetry.lock (root), so the bare patterns are unambiguous.
evidence: JenkinsPipelineUtils vars/utils.groovy:33-41 via the gitblit mirror (`it.path ==~ pattern`, Groovy full-match)
JenkinsPipelineUtils vars/utils.groovy:33-41 (read via gitblit this pass)

items.description: Gate only: no FORCE or rebuild build parameter is added. To force a rebuild the operator replays the job from a commit that touched an input, or pushes a trivial change to `support/iac-image/`.
items.rationale: Full diff of Jenkinsfile.iac-image against the slice base shows no properties([...]) or parameters block added -- the only change is the import, the if/else around the existing kaniko stage, and imageBuildRequired(). No FORCE/force parameter exists.
evidence: git diff a8506f53..d1005fa -- Jenkinsfile.iac-image (full diff read)

items.area: Pillar B — the tree lands in-repo (R3, ruling)
items.description: Every file that was in `pvginkel/IaCAgent` is at `support/iac-agent/<same relative path>` — sibling of `support/iac-image/` — and IaCAgent's root files did not land at the Ansible repo root. The move itself is a pure rename: the commits that land the tree change no file's content. The R4 drift fixes ship separately, on top of it.
items.rationale: `diff -rq /work/IaCAgent support/iac-agent --exclude=.git` reports exactly 5 files differing (README.md, bin/iac, bin/iac-impl, bin/send_message.py, etc/cron.d/iac-prune -- all PC's documented drift edits) and 0 files missing on either side; every other one of the tree's 13 entries is byte-identical. IaCAgent's root files (README.md, .gitignore, install.sh) all landed under support/iac-agent/, not at the Ansible repo root -- confirmed by directory listing.
evidence: /work/IaCAgent tree at 973d330: 13 files (bin/, etc/, systemd/, install.sh, README.md, .gitignore)
find support/iac-agent -type f (13 files, matches /work/IaCAgent's tree)

items.description: The IaCAgent commit history is preserved in the move: every IaCAgent commit is present in the Ansible repo with its original author, date and message and is reachable from `main`. A tree whose history starts at this slice does not satisfy this.
items.rationale: /work/IaCAgent's main branch holds exactly 28 commits. `git log -- support/iac-agent/` in this repo shows 31 commits touching that path: the 28 history-preserved originals plus PB's repoint commit is outside the path and PC's 3 drift-fix commits are inside it (7461c61, 60ca07b, d1005fa) -- 28+3=31, matches. Spot-checked author/date/subject for the 5 most recent of the 28 against /work/IaCAgent's own log: identical (Pieter van Ginkel, 2026-06-12/13 dates, same subjects). All 28 are reachable from main (this repo's default branch, ff-only merge per run_loop.py:1949).

items.area: Pillar B — the role reads it in place (R3, R4)
items.description: The `iac_agent` role reads the tree in place: `iac_agent_local_checkout` points at the in-repo path, no sibling checkout is consulted, and the role resolves correctly both from the operator's `/work/Ansible` and from the fresh clone `iac-impl` makes inside the container.
items.rationale: ansible/roles/iac_agent/defaults/main.yml:7 now reads `{{ playbook_dir }}/../../support/iac-agent` -- relative to ansible/playbooks/, so it resolves under both the operator's /work/Ansible and iac-impl's fresh in-container clone alike (no sibling checkout assumed by the path). tasks/main.yml:68,89 both still reference {{ iac_agent_local_checkout }} unmodified -- the variable is the role's only integration point and needed no other edit.

items.description: The drift R4 names is fixed inside `support/iac-agent/`, the tree the slice moves: `grep modern-app-dev support/iac-agent/` returns nothing; nothing in the tree still presents itself as a separate repo beside Ansible; its Jenkinsfile list matches the `Jenkinsfile.*` set the repo actually has; and its bind-mount list matches what `bin/iac` actually mounts. Sync and install paths are updated where any exist — the role's (V08); the tree's own installer is self-relative and owes none.

items.area: Pillar B — no host-side regression (R6 precondition)
items.description: The host-side layout is unchanged, so the merge is provable by a near-no-op apply: `install.sh` still materializes the same files at the same paths, and everything `bin/iac` bind-mounts into the container still resolves.
items.rationale: install.sh (unmodified by PB/PC except the 4 PC content edits, all prose/comment lines) still materializes the same targets at the same host paths -- read in full, no path changed. Live read-only check this pass: /opt/IaCAgent on srviac (ansible ad-hoc `command -a 'ls -la /opt/IaCAgent'` against the iac_agent group) still holds the pre-slice content (README.md dated Jun 12, no PC edits present) -- confirming the host is untouched and the operator's parity apply is real, pending work, not a no-op that already happened.

items.area: Pillar B — parity handed to the operator (R6, ruling)

items.rationale: Not run -- the role has side effects (installs software, syncs files onto a live host), so per slice-testing-strategy.md section 3 this is not run from here even in --check mode. Command below follows docs/live-infra-access.md's canonical shape.

items.area: Pillar B — the slice stops before the fallback removal (ruling, N5)
items.description: The slice stops before `.kubecoder/config.yaml`: it still declares IaCAgent, `/work/IaCAgent` is still on disk, and the parity apply, the config removal and archiving `pvginkel/IaCAgent` are recorded as operator-owed rather than done.
items.rationale: .kubecoder/config.yaml:12 and Ansible.code-workspace:16 both still declare the IaCAgent entry (grep, this pass) -- neither was touched by this slice, matching the ruling that the fallback stays until parity is proven and the operator archives the repo.

items.area: R7 — the removed repo boundary followed through
items.description: `decisions.md` is updated if the IaCAgent location became doctrine, and the `update-architecture` agent is nudged for the removed repo boundary — the model still names `git:pvginkel/IaCAgent` as the `iac shim`'s source repository.
items.rationale: Not this phase's charter: docs/slice-doc-plan.md assigns decisions.md and the architecture nudge to the doc phase, which the driver runs after the test phase completes (run_loop.py: _run_phases -> completion_consult -> test phase -> doc phase). decisions.md:117 still names pvginkel/IaCAgent and ansible-architecture.yaml:338 still carries sourceRepository: git:pvginkel/IaCAgent (both confirmed unchanged, this pass) -- correctly untouched by this phase. Flagging for the doc phase: whether the tree's new home (support/iac-agent/ in this repo) rises to doctrine in decisions.md is its call per slice-doc-plan.md's 'standing rule' bar; the architecture nudge is owed regardless (removed repo boundary, per R7).
